claims: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II launch occurred at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II launch occurred at 22:24 GMT.
The Artemis II launch was from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B.
The Artemis II mission sends four astronauts on a 10-day crewed flyby around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission marks the first human lunar mission in over 50 years.
The crew of the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The mission duration of Artemis II is ~10 days.
The launch site of Artemis II is Kennedy Space Center, Florida (LC-39B).
The Artemis II mission was originally targeted for 2024.
The Artemis II schedule was shifted to February 2026.
The Artemis II schedule was finalized for April.
Artemis II delays were due to technical issues including a helium leak.
Artemis II delays were due to a battery issue in the Launch Abort System.
